title: Ethical Hacking Foundations
shortDescription: Build practical cybersecurity skills by learning the fundamentals of ethical hacking, network security, reconnaissance, scanning, and vulnerability assessment.
fullDescription:
Ethical Hacking Foundations is a practical beginner-friendly cybersecurity program designed to introduce learners to the core concepts, tools, and methodologies used in ethical hacking.

Participants will learn how attackers identify and assess potential weaknesses while developing the knowledge needed to defend systems and networks responsibly. The program covers cybersecurity fundamentals, Linux basics, networking concepts, reconnaissance and footprinting, host discovery, port scanning, service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, and introductory web security.

Through guided exercises and hands-on labs, learners will practice using industry-relevant security tools in controlled environments. The program emphasizes responsible security testing, ethical conduct, documentation, and understanding how vulnerabilities can be identified and mitigated.

By the end of the program, participants should have a solid foundation for continuing into more advanced areas such as penetration testing, security operations, vulnerability management, and web application security.
targetAudience: Beginners interested in cybersecurity and ethical hacking
certification: Certificate of Completion – Ethical Hacking Foundations

curriculumModules.title: Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking Fundamentals
topics: Setting Up a Safe Hacking Lab
curriculumModules.project: Build Your Cybersecurity Lab: Set up an isolated virtual environment containing an attacker machine and a deliberately vulnerable target, then document the network configuration and security objectives.

curriculumModules.title: Networking Fundamentals
curriculumModules.project: Network Mapping Project: Analyze a controlled lab network, identify hosts, network interfaces, gateways, IP addresses, and available services, then create a basic network map.

curriculumModules.title: Linux Fundamentals for Hackers
curriculumModules.project: Linux Security Administration Lab : Configure a Linux machine with multiple users, permissions, services, and network settings, then perform a basic security audit.

curriculumModules.title: Reconnaissance & OSINT
curriculumModules.project: Target Reconnaissance Report:  Conduct passive reconnaissance on an authorized training target and produce a professional report containing domains, subdomains, DNS information, technologies, and other publicly available information.

curriculumModules.title: Host Discovery & Network Scanning
curriculumModules.project: Network Discovery Assessment: Perform host discovery and port scanning against a controlled lab network, identify active systems and exposed services, and produce a structured scanning report.

curriculumModules.title: Service Enumeration
curriculumModules.project: Service Enumeration Report: Enumerate the services running on an authorized vulnerable machine, identify service versions and technologies, and document potential security weaknesses.

curriculumModules.title: Vulnerability Assessment
curriculumModules.project: Vulnerability Assessment: Assess a deliberately vulnerable system using appropriate security tools, validate selected findings, rank vulnerabilities by severity, and produce a professional vulnerability assessment report.

curriculumModules.title: Web Application Security
curriculumModules.project: Web Application Security Assessment: Assess a deliberately vulnerable application such as OWASP Juice Shop, identify selected vulnerabilities, collect evidence, explain their impact, and provide remediation recommendations.

curriculumModules.title: Password Security & Authentication
curriculumModules.project: Authentication Security Audit: Analyze a controlled application's authentication system, identify weaknesses in password and login controls, and develop recommendations for improving authentication security.

curriculumModules.title: Ethical Hacking Methodology & Final Assessment
curriculumModules.project: Complete Ethical Hacking Assessment: Perform a full security assessment against an authorized vulnerable lab environment from reconnaissance through reporting, then present the findings and recommended remediation measures.

curriculumModules.title: Complete Ethical Hacking Assessment
curriculumModules.project: NEXUS Red Team Security Assessment:  Students perform a complete ethical hacking assessment against an authorized, deliberately vulnerable lab environment. They must progress through reconnaissance, discovery, scanning, enumeration, vulnerability assessment, analysis, and documentation, then produce and present a professional penetration-testing-style report containing their findings, evidence, risk ratings, and recommended remediation measures.

requirements: Ability to attend practical training and complete assignments
No previous ethical hacking experience required
